??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Sit down, *Player*. No, there. You may read over my shoulder today. Today only.
    - Your marks are in the book. In my hand, not yours. Yours was adequate.
    - Still writing. Still sharp. The quill, I mean.
    - Ah. Someone who knows not to touch the stack.
    - Well? The book does not write itself. I have asked it to.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about the Tide Book.
        - *Choice:* How is Halvard?
        - *Choice:* Goodbye.
    - Ailsa. Keeper of the Tide Book, forty-six years. I came here at seventeen to copy for old Keeper Innes, the same spring Varro became a warden.
    - We are the last two from those days. He trusts my memory more than his own. I trust his eyes more than mine. Between us we used to make one very good warden.
    - You want a tide? Very well. The great storm of forty years ago, the autumn moon. Turn at the fourth hour past midnight, water two steps over the top ring of the quay, wind north-west and rising.
    - Written in by a warden whose spelling I shall not discuss. There. Now you have heard me recite. Very few people ask.
    - The oldest pages are the first camp's: Savage tally marks and a careful Magician hand. They have been rebound so often the spine is younger than the wardens.
    - The later volumes stand on the long shelf in the back room, where it is dry. The current one lies here, under the window. Every tide since the first camp. Every one.
    - Halvard is very well. He straightened my notes at eleven and again at half past. I put them crooked again each time. It is one of the small pleasures of my day. Do not tell him.
    - Off you go. Mind the stack on your way past.
